validation_repairs: First run passed 316 web Rust tests, then Clippy refused the equivalent >=MAX+1 transaction target bound; changed to >MAX and repeated Rust/Clippy validation.

Second run passed Rust, Clippy and four original-desktop tests. One existing no-project panel regression failed because undefined epochs incorrectly counted as a valid catalog; added an explicit catalog presence guard. All 636 JavaScript tests and the native binary were rerun with exact inherited Rust hashes. The following real API cycle check exposed hidden worker validation errors; original status/message propagation was fixed and a new full Rust/Clippy/desktop/JavaScript/native build run passed.
limits: Metadata-only qualification with small native JSON and bounded crash-recovery fixtures. No rendered GPU, long media, physical pointer/DPI or hostile-media soak acceptance.

Native folder tree <=512 folders/16 levels/256 KiB; per operation asset JSON read/staging <=16 MiB, <=128 affected assets, <=64 selected batch assets; global prepared stage admission <=16 directories, unconfirmed completions <=4096/8 MiB. Unknown orphan stages are preserved and admission refuses instead of deleting foreign work.

Preparation runs on the existing one-worker/one-pending asset queue. Final commit checks bounded file witnesses and installs metadata; roster <=10000 stats and receipt-capacity <=4096 stats remain filesystem latency, not a claim of zero actor IO.
Shared web writers cooperate through the catalog/global locks. Concurrent native desktop writers do not honor those locks; sequential native compatibility only.

No new NAS mount or browser/environment installation. The 14 TB ds4 media catalog remains separately qualified. No local build/render/test fleet; browser checks used the existing Windows browser and one temporary tab.

The separate main editor retained five unsaved MoveClips and its Undo history. This evidence closes the bounded native folder workflow; the shared-library capability remains partial for physical placement/drag and broader offline/lifecycle acceptance.
